mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the previous month signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where CPIAUCSL annualized increase exceeds 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous three months signals a tightening labor market, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5pp over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where RSAFS increases by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% month-over-month signals a weakening supply side, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO decreases by more than 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is rising, it signals a potential overheating economy with accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where FEDFUNDS is below 1% and CPIAUCSL is rising.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over the previous month signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the months where PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) and Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a broad-based demand expansion, which boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase > 1% MoM
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where both HOUST and RSAFS increase by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3% and GDP (GDPC1) growth is below 2% year-over-year, it signals a restrictive monetary policy in a slowing economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: restrictive monetary policy in slowing economy
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where FEDFUNDS is above 3% and GDPC1 YoY growth is below 2%.
